lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Order least to greatest: 1/2, 1/8, 1/3 (same wholes).

FEEDBACK
1/8; 1/3; 1/2.

WATCH FOR
Comparing numerators only (thinking 1/8 > 1/3 because 8>3) reverses the truth for unit fractions.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Compare twelve pairs of unit fractions with diagrams or number lines. Write <, > or = and a one-line reason naming part size.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Compare twelve pairs of unit fractions with diagrams or number lines. Write <, > or = and a one-line reason naming part size. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: 1/8; 1/3; 1/2. Reasoning: I used compare by attending to unit fraction and explain why it matters rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Comparing numerators only (thinking 1/8 > 1/3 because 8>3) reverses the truth for unit fractions. Correction: 1/8; 1/3; 1/2. Why: the correction restores accurate use of compare.

Parent: Likely misconception: Comparing numerators only (thinking 1/8 > 1/3 because 8>3) reverses the truth for unit fractions. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.
